purpose: Same-author style-embedding surface. Embeds passages with a frozen style encoder (LUAR default; Wegmann, StyleDistance, mUAR and STAR selectable via --model) and reports the cosine-similarity DISTRIBUTION across windows — internal consistency (single), consistency with a baseline voice centroid (two-corpus), or where the target's candidate-similarity falls relative to an impostor pool (n-way, descriptive). StyleDistance (arXiv:2410.12757) is a more content-independent manifold than LUAR; mUAR (arXiv:2509.16531) is a multilingual authorship encoder. STAR (arXiv:2310.11081) is the style scorer the author-style-transfer literature reports; its weights declare no license, so it loads only with --allow-undeclared-license. Cross-encoder cosines are NOT comparable. The default stays LUAR (no silent flip). Refuses any identity / AI verdict; ships PROVISIONAL with no threshold, per encoder.
use_when: You want a learned-manifold complement to the scalar voice-coherence signals (voice_distance, idiolect_detector)
You want same-author-consistency evidence that needs no per-deployment training and no threshold
You want the embedding analogue of the general-imposters framing (target vs candidate vs impostor pool)
do_not_use_when: You need an identity verdict ("same person" / "different author") — the surface refuses it
You need an AI-vs-human call — this surface does not discriminate provenance
Windows are short (<~100 tokens) — style embeddings are fragile on short text; read the distribution, not single windows
You want a general-imposters win/loss proportion — use general_imposters.py (this is descriptive only)

compute.cost_note: loads a ~0.5–1.4 GB style encoder (LUAR / Wegmann / StyleDistance / mUAR / STAR); CPU-feasible, GPU optional <2 GB VRAM

examples.description: N-way embedding analogue (target vs candidate vs impostors)
STAR encoder, for comparison with published style-transfer numbers (no declared license)
